warsh: Kevin Warsh became Chair of the Federal Reserve in May 2026. He previously served on the Fed's Board of Governors from 2006 to 2011, including during the 2008 financial crisis, and later worked as a fellow at Stanford University's Hoover Institution. Earlier in his career he worked in investment banking and on economic policy at the White House.
powell: Jerome Powell served as Chair of the Federal Reserve from 2018 to 2026, after joining the Fed's Board of Governors in 2012. A lawyer by training, he worked in investment banking and private equity and served at the Treasury Department under President George H. W. Bush. As Chair he led the Fed through the pandemic and the rise in inflation that followed.
yellen: Janet Yellen was Chair of the Federal Reserve from 2014 to 2018, the first woman to hold the job. An economist who taught at the University of California, Berkeley, she earlier chaired the White House Council of Economic Advisers, led the San Francisco Fed and served as Fed Vice Chair. She later served as the 78th Secretary of the Treasury, from 2021 to 2025.
bernanke: Ben Bernanke was Chair of the Federal Reserve from 2006 to 2014. A former Princeton University economics professor who studied the Great Depression, he led the Fed through the 2008 financial crisis and the slow recovery that followed. In 2022 he shared the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for research on banks and financial crises.
greenspan: Alan Greenspan was Chair of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006, one of the longest tenures in the job, serving under four presidents. An economist and former business consultant, he earlier chaired the White House Council of Economic Advisers under President Gerald Ford. His years as Chair spanned the 1987 stock market crash and the long expansion of the 1990s.
volcker: Paul Volcker was Chair of the Federal Reserve from 1979 to 1987, appointed by President Carter and reappointed by President Reagan. He is best known for raising interest rates sharply to bring down the high inflation of the late 1970s. He earlier led the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and later advised President Obama on the economy. He died in 2019.
karp: Alex Karp co-founded Palantir Technologies in 2003 and has led it as chief executive since its early years. Palantir builds data analysis software used by government agencies and businesses, and its shares are publicly traded. Karp holds a law degree from Stanford University and a doctorate from Goethe University in Frankfurt, Germany.
jassy: Andy Jassy became President and CEO of Amazon in July 2021, succeeding founder Jeff Bezos. He joined Amazon in 1997 and built and led Amazon Web Services, the company's cloud computing business, for many years. Amazon runs online shopping, cloud services, devices, streaming and advertising businesses.
abel: Greg Abel became CEO of Berkshire Hathaway at the start of 2026, succeeding Warren Buffett. He previously led Berkshire Hathaway Energy and, as vice chairman, oversaw the company's businesses outside insurance. Berkshire owns a wide range of companies, from railroads and utilities to insurance and well-known consumer brands.
pichai: Sundar Pichai has been CEO of Google since 2015 and of its parent company, Alphabet, since 2019. He joined Google in 2004 and led products including the Chrome browser and Android. Alphabet's businesses include Search, YouTube, Google Cloud and artificial intelligence research.
nadella: Satya Nadella became CEO of Microsoft in 2014 and its chairman in 2021. He joined the company in 1992 and earlier ran its cloud and enterprise group. Under his leadership Microsoft has focused on cloud computing, business software and artificial intelligence.
zuckerberg: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and has led the company as CEO ever since. The company renamed itself Meta in 2021. It runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, and works on virtual reality and artificial intelligence. He grew up in New York.
dimon: Jamie Dimon has led JPMorgan Chase as chief executive since the mid-2000s, making him one of the longest-serving heads of a major U.S. bank. JPMorgan Chase is the largest bank in the United States by assets. His yearly letter to shareholders is widely read across the financial world.
furner: John Furner became President and CEO of Walmart in February 2026, succeeding Doug McMillon. He started at Walmart as an hourly store associate and later led Sam's Club and Walmart U.S. Walmart is the world's largest retailer by revenue. He is a graduate of the University of Arkansas.
mcinerney: Ryan McInerney became CEO of Visa in February 2023 after serving as the company's president. Before Visa he was an executive at JPMorgan Chase, where he led the consumer bank. Visa runs one of the world's largest payment networks, connecting card holders, merchants and banks.
duato: Joaquin Duato became CEO of Johnson & Johnson in January 2022 and later also became its chairman. Born in Spain, he joined the company in 1989 and held leadership roles in its pharmaceutical business. Johnson & Johnson focuses on medicines and medical technology.
decker: Ted Decker became CEO of The Home Depot in 2022 and later added the role of chair. He joined the company in 2000 and held senior roles in strategy, merchandising and operations. The Home Depot is the largest home improvement retailer in the United States.
moynihan: Brian Moynihan has been CEO of Bank of America since 2010 and chairman since 2014. A lawyer by training, he joined the bank through its purchase of FleetBoston. Bank of America is one of the largest banks in the United States, serving consumers, businesses and investors.
su: Lisa Su became CEO of AMD in 2014 and later also became its chair. An electrical engineer with a doctorate from MIT, she earlier worked at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale. AMD designs processors and graphics chips used in personal computers, game consoles and data centers.
benioff: Marc Benioff co-founded Salesforce in 1999 and serves as its chair and CEO. Salesforce sells cloud software that helps businesses manage sales, customer service and marketing. Before founding the company, Benioff spent more than a decade at Oracle.
robbins: Chuck Robbins became CEO of Cisco in 2015 and chair in 2017. He joined the company in 1997 and led its worldwide sales before taking the top job. Cisco makes networking equipment, security products and software that connect offices, homes and data centers.
pick: Ted Pick became CEO of Morgan Stanley in January 2024, succeeding James Gorman, and later also became chairman. He joined the firm in 1990 and led its institutional securities business. Morgan Stanley is a global investment bank and wealth management firm.
fraser: Jane Fraser became CEO of Citigroup in 2021, the first woman to lead one of the largest U.S. banks, and later also became its chair. She joined Citi in 2004 and led several of its businesses, including Latin America. Citi is a global bank with operations in many countries.
stankey: John Stankey became CEO of AT&T in 2020 and later also became its chairman. He joined the company in 1985 and held many senior roles, including running WarnerMedia. AT&T provides wireless, fiber internet and other communications services. He grew up in Los Angeles.
amon: Cristiano Amon became CEO of Qualcomm in 2021. Born in Brazil and trained as an electrical engineer, he joined Qualcomm in 1995 and led its chip business. Qualcomm designs processors and wireless technology used in smartphones, cars and connected devices.
khosrowshahi: Dara Khosrowshahi became CEO of Uber in 2017 after leading the travel company Expedia for about twelve years. Born in Iran, he moved to the United States as a child. Uber runs ride-hailing, food delivery and freight services in many countries.
niccol: Brian Niccol became chairman and CEO of Starbucks in September 2024. He previously led Chipotle Mexican Grill and earlier worked at Taco Bell and Procter & Gamble. Starbucks runs and licenses coffee shops around the world. He grew up in Ohio.
ortberg: Kelly Ortberg became President and CEO of Boeing in August 2024. An engineer by training, he earlier led Rockwell Collins, a maker of aircraft electronics, for many years. Boeing builds commercial airplanes as well as defense and space systems.
cook: Tim Cook was CEO of Apple from August 2011 until August 2026, when he handed the role to John Ternus and became Executive Chairman. He joined Apple in 1998 to run its operations and supply chain. As CEO he oversaw new products such as the Apple Watch and AirPods and the growth of Apple's services.
jobs: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976. After leaving in 1985, he founded NeXT and led Pixar, then returned to Apple in 1997 and served as CEO until August 2011. His later years at Apple brought the iMac, iPod, iPhone and iPad. He died in October 2011.
musk: Elon Musk is CEO of Tesla and of SpaceX, which he founded in 2002. He joined Tesla as an early investor and chairman in 2004 and became its CEO in 2008. Tesla makes electric vehicles and energy products, and SpaceX builds rockets and spacecraft and runs the Starlink satellite internet service.
abbott: Greg Abbott has been Governor of Texas since 2015. A Republican, he previously served as Texas Attorney General and as a justice on the Texas Supreme Court. As governor he signs or vetoes bills passed by the Legislature and leads the state's emergency response.
cox: Spencer Cox has been Governor of Utah since 2021. A Republican and a lawyer from the small town of Fairview, he previously served as Utah's lieutenant governor, in the Utah House of Representatives and as a county commissioner.
desantis: Ron DeSantis has been Governor of Florida since 2019. A Republican, he earlier served three terms in the U.S. House of Representatives and was a lawyer in the U.S. Navy. Florida's governor leads the state's executive branch and its response to hurricanes and other emergencies.
ferguson: Bob Ferguson became Governor of Washington in January 2025. A Democrat, he previously served three terms as the state's Attorney General and earlier sat on the King County Council. He grew up in Seattle.
green: Josh Green has been Governor of Hawaii since December 2022. A Democrat and a physician, he earlier served as the state's lieutenant governor and in both the Hawaii House and Senate. He first worked in Hawaii as a rural doctor on the Big Island.
hobbs: Katie Hobbs became Governor of Arizona in January 2023. A Democrat and a former social worker, she previously served as Arizona Secretary of State and in the state Legislature. She grew up in Phoenix.
hochul: Kathy Hochul became Governor of New York in 2021, the first woman to hold the office. A Democrat, she earlier served as lieutenant governor and represented a western New York district in the U.S. House.
kemp: Brian Kemp has been Governor of Georgia since 2019. A Republican, he previously served as Georgia's Secretary of State and in the state Senate, and ran small businesses in construction and real estate.
moore: Wes Moore became Governor of Maryland in January 2023. A Democrat, he is an Army veteran, Rhodes Scholar and author, and earlier led the Robin Hood Foundation, an anti-poverty nonprofit in New York.
newsom: Gavin Newsom has been Governor of California since 2019. A Democrat, he previously served as the state's lieutenant governor and as mayor of San Francisco. He grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area and started several businesses before entering politics.
reynolds: Kim Reynolds has been Governor of Iowa since 2017, the first woman to hold the office. A Republican, she earlier served as lieutenant governor, in the Iowa Senate and as a county treasurer.
sanders: Sarah Huckabee Sanders became Governor of Arkansas in January 2023, the first woman to hold the office. A Republican, she previously served as White House Press Secretary. Her father, Mike Huckabee, was also governor of the state.
barrasso: John Barrasso has represented Wyoming in the U.S. Senate since 2007 and became Senate Majority Whip in 2025. A Republican and an orthopedic surgeon, he earlier served in the Wyoming Senate. Before entering politics, he practiced medicine in Casper, Wyoming, for more than two decades.
blackburn: Marsha Blackburn has represented Tennessee in the U.S. Senate since 2019, the first woman elected to the Senate from the state. A Republican, she earlier served eight terms in the U.S. House. Before Congress, she ran a marketing business and served in the Tennessee State Senate.
booker: Cory Booker has represented New Jersey in the U.S. Senate since 2013. A Democrat, he earlier served as mayor of Newark. He studied at Stanford University and was a Rhodes Scholar. He is the first Black senator elected from New Jersey, and earlier served on the Newark City Council.
cruz: Ted Cruz has represented Texas in the U.S. Senate since 2013. A Republican and a lawyer, he previously served as Solicitor General of Texas and argued cases before the U.S. Supreme Court. Before that, he served as a law clerk to Chief Justice William Rehnquist.
durbin: Dick Durbin has represented Illinois in the U.S. Senate since 1997 and serves as Senate Democratic Whip. A Democrat and a lawyer, he earlier served seven terms in the U.S. House. He grew up in East St. Louis, Illinois, and earned his law degree from Georgetown University.
grassley: Chuck Grassley has represented Iowa in the U.S. Senate since 1981 and serves as President pro tempore of the Senate. A Republican and a farmer, he earlier served in the U.S. House and the Iowa Legislature. He grew up in Iowa.
hickenlooper: John Hickenlooper has represented Colorado in the U.S. Senate since 2021. A Democrat and a former geologist, he co-founded a Denver brewpub and later served as mayor of Denver and as Governor of Colorado. He grew up near Philadelphia and moved to Colorado in the 1980s.
klobuchar: Amy Klobuchar has represented Minnesota in the U.S. Senate since 2007, the first woman elected to the Senate from the state. A Democrat and a lawyer, she earlier served as the chief prosecutor for Hennepin County. She grew up in Plymouth, Minnesota.
lummis: Cynthia Lummis has represented Wyoming in the U.S. Senate since 2021. A Republican and a rancher, she earlier served as Wyoming State Treasurer and represented the state in the U.S. House. She grew up on her family's ranch near Cheyenne, Wyoming, and later earned a law degree.
murphy: Chris Murphy has represented Connecticut in the U.S. Senate since 2013. A Democrat and a lawyer, he earlier served in the U.S. House and in the Connecticut General Assembly. He grew up in Wethersfield, Connecticut, and earned his law degree from the University of Connecticut.
paul: Rand Paul has represented Kentucky in the U.S. Senate since 2011. A Republican and an eye surgeon, he is the son of former Texas congressman Ron Paul. Before the Senate, he practiced as an ophthalmologist in Bowling Green, Kentucky, for nearly two decades.
schiff: Adam Schiff has represented California in the U.S. Senate since December 2024. A Democrat and a former federal prosecutor, he earlier served more than two decades in the U.S. House. He grew up in Massachusetts and California and earned his law degree from Harvard Law School.
schumer: Chuck Schumer has represented New York in the U.S. Senate since 1999 and leads the Senate Democrats. He served as Majority Leader from 2021 to 2025, and earlier served in the U.S. House and the New York State Assembly.
thune: John Thune has represented South Dakota in the U.S. Senate since 2005 and became Senate Majority Leader in January 2025. A Republican, he earlier served in the U.S. House. He grew up in Murdo, South Dakota, and earlier led the state's railroad office and its municipal league.
jeffries: Hakeem Jeffries has represented a Brooklyn-based district in the U.S. House since 2013 and has led the House Democrats since 2023. A lawyer, he earlier served in the New York State Assembly. He grew up in Brooklyn.
johnson: Mike Johnson has represented Louisiana's 4th District in the U.S. House since 2017 and became Speaker of the House in October 2023. A Republican, he earlier practiced constitutional law and served in the Louisiana Legislature.
bessent: Scott Bessent became the 79th Secretary of the Treasury in January 2025. Before government service he spent decades as an investor, including at Soros Fund Management, and founded the investment firm Key Square Group. The Treasury manages the federal government's finances, borrowing and tax collection.
hegseth: Pete Hegseth became Secretary of Defense in January 2025; the department is now also called the Department of War. An Army National Guard veteran who served in Iraq and Afghanistan, he earlier worked as a television host.
lutnick: Howard Lutnick became the 41st Secretary of Commerce in February 2025. He previously led the financial services firm Cantor Fitzgerald for about three decades. The Commerce Department covers trade, economic statistics, weather forecasting and technology standards.
rubio: Marco Rubio became the 72nd Secretary of State in January 2025. He earlier represented Florida in the U.S. Senate from 2011 to 2025 and served as Speaker of the Florida House of Representatives. The Secretary of State leads the country's diplomacy.
roberts: John Roberts has been Chief Justice of the United States since 2005, appointed by President George W. Bush. He earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit and, as a lawyer, argued many cases before the Supreme Court.
thomas: Clarence Thomas has served on the Supreme Court since 1991, appointed by President George H. W. Bush, and is its longest-serving current member. He earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit and chaired the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.
alito: Samuel Alito has served on the Supreme Court since 2006, appointed by President George W. Bush. He earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and as U.S. Attorney for New Jersey.
sotomayor: Sonia Sotomayor has served on the Supreme Court since 2009, appointed by President Obama, and is the Court's first Hispanic justice. She earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and as a federal trial judge in New York.
kagan: Elena Kagan has served on the Supreme Court since 2010, appointed by President Obama. She earlier served as U.S. Solicitor General, the government's top lawyer before the Court, and as dean of Harvard Law School.
gorsuch: Neil Gorsuch has served on the Supreme Court since 2017, appointed by President Trump. He earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, which sits in Denver, and worked at the Justice Department.
kavanaugh: Brett Kavanaugh has served on the Supreme Court since 2018, appointed by President Trump. He earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit and worked in the White House under President George W. Bush.
barrett: Amy Coney Barrett has served on the Supreme Court since 2020, appointed by President Trump. She earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and taught law at the University of Notre Dame.
jackson: Ketanji Brown Jackson has served on the Supreme Court since 2022, appointed by President Biden, and is the first Black woman on the Court. She earlier served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit, as a federal trial judge and as a federal public defender.
carter: Jimmy Carter was the 39th President of the United States, serving from 1977 to 1981. A Democrat, Navy veteran and peanut farmer, he earlier served as Governor of Georgia. After leaving office he received the 2002 Nobel Peace Prize for his humanitarian work. He died in December 2024 at age 100.
reagan: Ronald Reagan was the 40th President of the United States, serving two terms from 1981 to 1989. A Republican, he earlier worked as a film actor and served two terms as Governor of California. He died in 2004.
bush41: George H. W. Bush was the 41st President of the United States, serving from 1989 to 1993. A Republican and a World War II Navy pilot, he earlier served as Vice President under Ronald Reagan, as CIA Director and as U.S. ambassador to the United Nations. He died in 2018.
clinton: Bill Clinton was the 42nd President of the United States, serving two terms from 1993 to 2001. A Democrat, he earlier served as Governor of Arkansas and as the state's Attorney General. He was born in Hope, Arkansas.
bush43: George W. Bush was the 43rd President of the United States, serving two terms from 2001 to 2009. A Republican, he earlier served as Governor of Texas. He is the son of the 41st President, George H. W. Bush.
obama: Barack Obama was the 44th President of the United States, serving two terms from 2009 to 2017. A Democrat, he earlier represented Illinois in the U.S. Senate and taught constitutional law. He received the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize.
trump: Donald Trump is the 45th and 47th President of the United States, serving from 2017 to 2021 and again since January 2025. A Republican, he previously ran a real estate business and hosted the television show The Apprentice.
biden: Joe Biden was the 46th President of the United States, serving from 2021 to 2025. A Democrat, he earlier served eight years as Vice President under Barack Obama and represented Delaware in the U.S. Senate for 36 years.
jefferson: Philip Jefferson has served on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors since May 2022 and became Vice Chair in September 2023. An economist who studies poverty and the labor market, he earlier taught at Swarthmore College and served as vice president for academic affairs and dean of faculty at Davidson College. He also worked as a research economist at the Federal Reserve Board early in his career.
bowman: Michelle Bowman has served on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors since November 2018 and became Vice Chair for Supervision in June 2025, leading the Fed's oversight of banks. She earlier served as Kansas State Bank Commissioner and was a vice president of a community bank in Kansas. She was the first governor appointed to fill the Board seat reserved for someone with community banking experience.
barr: Michael Barr has served on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors since July 2022. He was Vice Chair for Supervision from 2022 to 2025, leading the Fed's oversight of banks. A lawyer and former dean of the Ford School of Public Policy at the University of Michigan, he earlier served as an Assistant Secretary of the Treasury, where he helped shape the Dodd-Frank financial reform law.
lisacook: Lisa Cook has served on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors since May 2022, the first Black woman to serve on the Board. An economist, she earlier taught at Michigan State University and served on the White House Council of Economic Advisers staff. Her research covers economic growth, innovation and international economics.
waller: Christopher Waller has served on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors since December 2020. An economist, he earlier served as executive vice president and director of research at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and taught at the University of Notre Dame and other universities. His research focuses on monetary policy and how central banks work.
kennedy: John F. Kennedy was the 35th President of the United States, serving from 1961 until his assassination in November 1963. A Democrat and World War II Navy veteran, he earlier represented Massachusetts in both the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate.
eisenhower: Dwight D. Eisenhower was the 34th President of the United States, serving two terms from 1953 to 1961. A Republican and five-star Army general, he served as Supreme Commander of the Allied Expeditionary Force in Europe during World War II and as the first Supreme Allied Commander Europe of NATO. He died in 1969.
